To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we cloned, sequenced and expressed the cDNA coding for human cystatin C, a potent inhibitor of the cysteine proteinases, cathepsins B and L.
the cDNA coding for human cystatin C was cloned, sequenced, and the recombinant protein produced in E. coli.

the human cysteatin C cDNA was cloned and sequenced, that the deduced protein sequence confirmed the protein sequence of the cystein proteinase inhibitor isolated from human urine and that the sequence differed from the sequence of cystatin amyloid.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the isolation of cDNA clones coding for cystatin C from a human placental λgt11 cDNAlibrary and with the sequence analysis of one of these clones.
the molecular cloning and sequence analysis.
the isolation and characterization of a human cDNA clone for the cysteine protein inhibitor cystatin C and the determination of the amino acid sequence of the precursor of this inhibitor.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the sequence of the human cystatin C precursor deduced from the cDNA sequence and the sequence of the mature cystatin C from urine are identical, but that the sequence of cystatin deposited as amyloid is different in one position.
the cystatin C gene is expressed in the brain, in the liver and in the kidneys.
the cystatin C gene is located on the short arm of chromosome 20, and that the gene product is a 120 amino acid polypeptide which is secreted and which has a cysteine proteinases inhibitor activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cDNA coding for cystatin C is now available, which will allow us to study the regulation of the cystatin gene in different tissues and in different physiological and pathological conditions.
the human cysteatin C gene is located at chromosome 20 and that the cystatin C protein is a 120 amino acid polypeptide with a hydrophobic signal peptide.
the cystatin C precursor gene has a 5'-untranslated region of 45 base pairs, a 3'-untranslated region (3'-UTR) of 102 base pairs, and a coding region of 630 base pairs.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of recombinant DNA technology to study the structure and function of the cysteine proteinases and their inhibitors is a powerful approach that will provide important information about this class of enzymes.
the human cystatin C gene is a good model for the study of cystatin genes in other species.
the use of the human cystatin C gene as a biomarker for Alzheimer’s disease is questionable, and further research is needed to determine the role of cystatin C in AD.
